_comment: Cyber campaign tracker (collector/campaigns.py). Small cyber incidents are linked into suspected campaigns and read through an adversary lens: if an enemy is doing this on purpose, what is it trying to achieve, what would it hit next, and what would it mean for the family. Every output is a hypothesis to test, never a confirmed attribution.

water.name: water supply
water.for_us: Tampering with water treatment usually ends in boil-water notices or supply cuts for a few days.

action.action: Keep two days of bottled water for everyone, and the pets.
action.reason: It covers a boil-water notice or a short supply cut while the problem is fixed.

food.name: food and cold storage
food.for_us: Spoiled chilled and frozen stock means gaps on supermarket shelves for days.

action.action: Keep a week of pantry food that needs no fridge.
action.reason: It rides out empty chilled and frozen shelves without joining any panic buying.

finance.name: banks and payments
finance.for_us: Card payments, EFTPOS or online banking can be down for hours.

action.reason: Cash still buys fuel and food when cards and banking apps are down.

energy.name: power and gas
energy.for_us: Power cuts, sometimes over a wide area.

action.action: Check the torch, power banks and battery radio work.
action.reason: They keep you informed and lit if the power goes out.

fuel.name: fuel and shipping
fuel.for_us: Delays in fuel deliveries and higher prices at the bowser.

action.action: Keep the car at least half full.
action.reason: Fuel deliveries are the first thing to slip when ports or ships are disrupted.

telecom.name: phones and internet
telecom.for_us: Phones and internet could drop out, including emergency calls on one network.

action.action: Agree a family meeting point and save key numbers on paper.
action.reason: If calls and messages fail, everyone still knows where to go.

health.name: hospitals and health
health.for_us: Delays at hospitals, cancelled appointments and pharmacy problems.

action.action: Keep a few weeks of regular medicines.
action.reason: Pharmacy and hospital systems can be slow to recover after an attack.

government.name: government and defence
government.for_us: Usually no direct effect, but it can bring fake official messages and scams.

action.action: Only trust official messages you look up yourself, not links sent to you.
action.reason: Attackers often follow up with fake 'official' texts and emails.

transport.name: flights and transport
transport.for_us: Flight and transport delays, and slower deliveries.

action.action: Check flights and deliveries before relying on them this week.
action.reason: Transport systems often take days to fully recover.

it.name: software and online services
it.for_us: Apps and websites you use may be down, or quietly compromised.

action.action: Don't follow login or payment links in emails or texts; open the app or site yourself.
action.reason: Breaches of software suppliers are often followed by convincing scam messages.

supply_chain.name: hacking a supplier to reach many victims

Iran.motive: Hit back over the Gulf war and the US blockade by showing it can reach into allies' everyday services, without starting a shooting war with them.
next: Water and cold-storage systems in other allied countries, including Australia
Destructive wiper attacks if US or Israeli strikes resume
Iran.au_exposure: Australia is a close US ally and expelled Iran's ambassador in 2025. Australian water utilities and businesses use the same internet-connected controllers that have been hit overseas.
escalation: the same kind of attack reported in Australia or New Zealand
attacks that destroy data or damage equipment rather than just disrupt
an official warning from the Australian Cyber Security Centre naming Iran
new US or Israeli strikes on Iran

China.motive: Quietly plant footholds in allies' power, water, ports and phone networks, ready to switch them off if there is a war over Taiwan.
China.au_exposure: Australia's spy agencies have warned that Chinese state hackers have been found inside Australian infrastructure networks. This kind of campaign is designed to stay hidden until a crisis.
escalation: a warning about footholds found in Australian power, water or phone networks
rising tension or military drills around Taiwan
outages at several allied phone or power companies at once

Russia.motive: Pressure Europe and NATO over Ukraine with sabotage and disruption, and scare the public.
Russia.au_exposure: Australia supports Ukraine, so government websites and some businesses have been targeted before, mostly with nuisance attacks.
escalation: overload attacks on Australian government or bank websites
attacks that damage equipment in Europe
a NATO-Russia clash

North Korea.motive: Steal money, mostly cryptocurrency, to fund weapons programs.
North Korea.au_exposure: Mainly a risk to Australians who hold crypto, and to tech workers targeted with fake job offers.
escalation: a large theft from an exchange Australians use
fake job offers aimed at Australian tech workers

Criminal gangs.motive: Money: ransom payments and selling stolen data.
next: Other customers of the same software suppliers
Data dumps followed by scam waves
Criminal gangs.au_exposure: Australian companies are hit by the same gangs regularly; stolen customer data fuels scam calls and texts.
escalation: an Australian company named as a victim
your details in a breach notice
a wave of scam messages using a brand name

Hacktivists.motive: Publicity for a cause, often working alongside a state.
next: Overloading government, bank and airport websites
Hacktivists.au_exposure: Australian government and council websites are regular targets of nuisance attacks.
escalation: attacks shifting from websites to equipment
a state publicly backing the group

unknown.motive: If this is deliberate, an attacker may be testing defences in one sector across several countries before a bigger strike, or wearing it down in the background of a wider conflict.
next: The same kind of target in more allied countries
A bigger attack on the same sector
unknown.au_exposure: Australia uses the same software and equipment as other allied countries, so a technique that works overseas often works here.
escalation: the same pattern showing up in Australia
a government naming who is behind it
attacks becoming destructive
